reason: The docs do call --bare the recommended mode. But it skips auto-discovery only: skills from an --add-dir folder still load, and MCP servers can be passed with --mcp-config. The API-key requirement applies only to the Anthropic API, since Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Foundry keep reading their own provider credentials. The claim states both points too broadly.
found: In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment ... or supply an apiKeyHelper in the --settings JSON. Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry continue to read their own provider credentials as usual.
suggested_fix: --bare is the documented recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls. It skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, CLAUDE.md and auto memory, though you can pass some of these back with flags such as --mcp-config, and --add-dir folders still supply skills. Because it never uses a subscription login, calls to the Anthropic API need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper, while Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry use their own provider credentials.

reason: The headless page says -p runs start in Manual mode from v2.1.302 when nothing sets a mode, and that a call needing approval is denied unless something approves it. It lists --allowedTools/permissions.allow rules, a PermissionRequest hook and --permission-prompt-tool as approvers, and says that in a -p run with no host the requests are denied. Caveats: if --permission-prompt-tool is set, the run waits for that host; some tools, such as AskUserQuestion, are denied even when an allow rule matches.
found: In a Manual mode claude -p run, a call that needs approval is denied unless something approves it, such as a PermissionRequest hook or a --permission-prompt-tool . With Claude Code v2.1.302 or later, claude -p runs start in Manual mode when nothing sets a permission mode .
